signals.title: USD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Cross-Asset Risk
signals.text: USD/CHF trades at 0.8167, maintaining its position above the SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.8085/0.7996/0.7920). The pair serves as the primary vehicle for the current G10 bilateral theme, with the USD outperforming the G10 average by +0.638% while CHF laggards at -0.481%. A massive 375bp Fed-SNB carry advantage (Fed 3.75% vs SNB 0.0%) provides the structural bid, while a +1.47% USD real rate vs -0.62% CHF real rate confirms the fundamental divergence. Despite wider Middle East war headlines, the lack of acute risk-off sentiment (VIX 17.7) prevents a CHF safe-haven bid from compressing the carry spread. Options market pricing shows extreme complacency with a +6.4% VRP (IV 12.2% vs HV30 5.8%), suggesting the move is unhedged. Risk: VIX breaks above 25, triggering a rapid unwinding of the 375bp carry trade and a return toward the SMA20 at 0.8085.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry + COT/Retail Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY at 163.73 is consolidating just below its recent multi-decade highs, holding firmly above the SMA20 at 162.30. The pair is underpinned by a 275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage (Fed 3.75% vs BoJ 1.0%), though technicals show consolidation ahead of the July 31 BoJ meeting. A significant positioning divergence is active: COT LF net short is extreme at -105,238 (28% long) while retail sentiment is 80% short, indicating both specs and retail are heavily fading the upside. Options markets remain wary with a -1.48 25d RR put skew, signalling that institutional desks are paying for downside protection against potential BoJ intervention. The positive CESI for JPY (+10) vs USD (+29) suggests domestic data is supporting JPY, even as the carry trade remains the dominant flow. Risk: BoJ delivers a surprise hawkish shift on July 31, triggering a massive short squeeze of the crowded JPY short position.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning + Economic Surprise Divergence
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1390, remaining technically heavy below its entire SMA cluster (SMA20 1.142 to SMA200 1.164). COT positioning shows specs are net short EUR (-74,637) with only 33.3% long, a view reinforced by a stark Economic Surprise Index (CESI) divergence where the US is at +29 beats vs the Eurozone's -43 misses. While the ECB bias remains hawkish for September, a 135bp carry deficit (Fed 3.75% vs ECB 2.4%) continues to favor the Greenback. Options markets are pricing a +2.6% VRP, indicating that realized volatility is significantly lower than implied, suggesting a slow-grind lower rather than a volatile breakdown. The 25d RR shows a mild -0.49 put skew, confirming the market remains biased toward EUR weakness in the medium term. Risk: ECB explicitly commits to a 50bp September hike, closing the real rate gap and forcing a cover of the COT short position.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning vs Data Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD at 0.6995 is caught between bullish speculative positioning and deteriorating fundamental data. COT LF net long is at +21,946 (63.2% long), yet the pair faces a strong negative CESI (-14 misses), suggesting the currency is failing to live up to market expectations. Despite a 60bp carry advantage for the AUD (RBA 4.35% vs Fed 3.75%), the pair is struggling to hold above its SMA50 at 0.7031. Options volatility is at an extreme with a +6.5% VRP (IV 12.5% vs HV30 6.0%) and a moderate -0.90 25d RR put skew, indicating that while specs are long in futures, the options market is aggressively hedging for a downside reversal. This conflict between long spec positioning and bearish options/data metrics creates an asymmetric risk profile to the downside. Risk: RBA shifts to a dovish hold at the August 11 meeting, invalidating the carry-support thesis.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Correlation Break + Technical Levels
signals.text: USD/CAD at 1.4081 has broken its historical relationship with energy markets, with its correlation to WTI Oil collapsing to -0.925 (z = -1.59σ) compared to a near-zero norm. While Oil has dropped -4.57% today to $88.0, USDCAD remains sidelined, holding below its SMA20 (1.4136) but above its SMA50 (1.4013). This decoupling suggests that the 150bp USD carry advantage (Fed 3.75% vs BoC 2.25%) and general USD strength (DXY 101.31) are currently more influential than commodity flows. Speculative positioning is heavily short CAD at -93,515 (20.6% long), yet the pair has failed to extend higher, suggesting a period of distribution. Watch the 1.4000 psychological support level for signs of a deeper correction if the USD-centric theme pauses. Risk: A sudden spike in Oil prices above $95/bbl restores the traditional correlation and triggers CAD short-covering.
